articles.title: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Donation and New AI Infrastructure
articles.summary:
Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing.
To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities.
NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell, an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide.
NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate, an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox.
Additionally, NVIDIA announced new components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine, NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot. These tools help teams deploy, manage and scale GPU infrastructure on Kubernetes for AI factories.
Together, these advancements mark a step forward in making Kubernetes the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale — empowering developers to build safer, more efficient AI infrastructure for the future.

articles.summary:
The AI Security Gap Hiding in Routine Maintenance
Abby Kearns | 10 November 2026
This blog was first published on November 9, 2026 at https://openssf.org/blog/2026/11/09/the-ai-security-gap-hiding-in-routine-maintenance/ and repurposed here with consent from the author.
Ask a security team what worries them about AI and you'll probably hear about supply chain attacks or prompt injection first. The Linux Foundation's new report, State of AI Impact on Software Security and Cybersecurity 2026, backs that up, with 93% of the security experts it surveyed concerned about supply chain attacks and 90% about prompt injection. Some of the report's most important findings, though, are about something a lot less dramatic: the everyday work of keeping software up to date.
LF Research surveyed 308 people working on security in companies and open source projects this summer, in research sponsored by OpenSSF, LF AI & Data, and ActiveState, where I'm CEO. Coming at it as an operator, I wasn't surprised by what they found, because every dependency a team adds comes with years of upkeep, and that work almost never gets staffed the way new features do.
Where teams feel least prepared
The survey asked practitioners how concerned they are about a long list of AI-related threats and how prepared they feel for each one, and for every single threat, concern came out ahead. articles.title: Git security vulnerabilities announced
articles.summary:
Today, the Git project is releasing new versions to address six security vulnerabilities. These include arbitrary code execution when recursively cloning a malicious repository, writes to unintended files, and memory corruption when processing merges or binary patches.
The fixes are included in Git 2.56.1, with backports to Git 2.55.1, 2.54.1, 2.53.1, 2.52.1, 2.51.3, and 2.50.2. We recommend updating to Git 2.56.1 or the patched release for your maintenance series, and updating any applications that bundle Git.
Vulnerabilities in Git
CVE-2026-111760: Code execution during recursive clones
Git checks paths before writing files into a working tree, including rejecting paths that would overwrite its own repository metadata. However, an integer truncation in Git’s index handling can cause an extremely long path to pass validation under one name and then be written using a shorter name.
An attacker can use this discrepancy to replace a submodule’s .git file with a symbolic link pointing to a directory containing malicious configuration or hooks. When Git subsequently uses that directory, it can execute attacker-controlled code during a recursive clone.
The fix rejects extremely long index entry paths before their lengths can be truncated.
[Advisory]

articles.title: N-able Takes N-central Offline as Researcher Drops Over 30 Zero-Days
articles.summary:
N-able on Monday took hosted N-central environments offline in response to a security researcher’s public disclosure of more than 30 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities.
“As a precautionary measure, we are temporarily taking our Hosted N-central environment offline while we take the necessary actions to secure the environment and implement appropriate remediation,” the company said.
While N-central and the related services remain inaccessible, N-able says it has made progress validating the flaws and creating a fix, which should roll out around midday on November 10.
On-premises N-central deployments should also be kept offline until patches are released, the company says.
“N-able Engineering continues to make progress on the N-central hotfix and associated validation activities. The work remains on track with no setbacks, and our teams are progressing as quickly as possible while maintaining the validation required for a safe remediation,” the company said.
N-able also pointed out that it has no evidence that the vulnerabilities have been exploited against its N-central environments.
The zero-day bugs were published on GitHub on Sunday by security researcher Sean Bales and have yet to be assigned CVE identifiers. Bales dubbed the flaws Able2Shell.

articles.title: Les physiciens ont vu un événement subatomique qui ne se produit qu’une fois sur 10 milliards
articles.summary:
Le grand collisionneur de hadrons (LHC) du CERN a beau être un tunnel immense de 27 kilomètres de long, ce qu’on y observe est infiniment petit. C’est le cas d’une particule subatomique dite « de beauté », composée d’un quark down et d’un antiquark « beauté » (aussi appelé bottom). La collaboration LHCb lui consacre une étude mise en ligne le 30 octobre sur le serveur arXiv et présentée au CERN le 3 novembre, qui doit encore être relue par d’autres chercheurs avant de paraître dans une revue scientifique.
Comme le détaille l’université de Cambridge, une équipe d’une vingtaine de physiciens britanniques, allemands, italiens, espagnols et néerlandais, menée par Harry Cliff, du laboratoire Cavendish de cette même université, a obtenu les premiers indices solides de la désintégration de cette particule en deux muons, un événement extrêmement rare qui ne se produit qu’une fois sur 10 milliards.
Mais de quoi s’agit-il exactement ? Lorsque cette particule nommée Bd (ou B0) se désintègre, ce qui se produit environ 1,5 millième de milliardième de seconde (1,5 picoseconde) après son apparition, l’antiquark beauté qu’elle contient se transforme le plus souvent en antiquark charmé, plus rarement en antiquark up. Ce sont des cousins plus légers, avec une charge électrique différente.

articles.title: Anthropic Rolls Out Mythos 5.2 With Improved Bug Hunting, Fewer Sandbox Escapes
articles.summary:
Anthropic on Monday released Claude Mythos 5.2, the latest version of its access-restricted AI model, and Mozilla says it roughly doubled the vulnerability discovery results of Mythos 5.1 in Firefox.
Mythos 5.2 and Claude Fable 5.2, which was released alongside it, share the same underlying model. The difference lies in the guardrails: Fable, which anyone can use, carries protections against cybersecurity and biology misuse, while Mythos ships without some of them.
Direct access to Mythos is reserved for vetted organizations, which can apply through Anthropic’s Cyber and Life Sciences Verification Programs.
“We’ve worked closely with the Anthropic team all year to harden Firefox with successive generations of Claude models, and each round has left fewer, subtler bugs to find. Even so, Mythos 5.2 roughly doubled the vulnerability discovery metrics of Mythos 5.1 across respective scanning campaigns,” said Brian Grinstead, distinguished engineer at Mozilla.
Internally, Anthropic measures progress with CVE Rediscovery, which gives a model the code of a project from before a known CVE was patched and checks whether the model spots the flaw without help.
In an October run covering 1,829 CVEs, Mythos 5.2 achieved a success rate of 89.6%. Mythos 5.1 scored 78.3%, and Opus 5.5, tested without safeguards, scored 81.3%.

articles.title: Speech Processing Pioneer Bishnu Saroop Atal Dies at 93
articles.summary:
Bishnu Saroop Atal
Acoustics and signal processing pioneer
Life Fellow, 93; died 19 August
Atal was an acoustics and signal processing researcher at Bell Labs in Murray Hill, N.J., and later at AT&T’s Shannon Laboratory, in Florham Park, N.J. His pioneering work on voice-coding techniques became the foundation for efficient, high-quality voice transmission over cellular networks. He received the 2013 IEEE Jack S. Kilby Signal Processing Medal for “fundamental and pioneering contributions to speech coding.”
He joined Bell Labs in 1961 as a communications researcher, and his early work there focused on speaker identification technology. During the 1960s he helped develop linear predictive coding, a powerful method for analyzing and compressing speech. LPC is now the most widely used method for encoding speech at a low bit rate.
Atal developed increasingly sophisticated low-bit-rate speech-coding techniques. They included multipulse LPC, which improved the quality of compressed speech.
Bishnu Saroop AtalNokia Bell Labs
He also worked with his colleague Manfred R. Schroeder to develop code-excited linear prediction, a method for producing high-quality speech at very low bit rates. CELP became a foundational technique in modern speech coding, letting digital communications systems carry voice using less bandwidth. The extra efficiency expanded cellular capacity, allowing wireless networks to handle more simultaneous calls.

articles.title: Google Fi is bringing back multiple cell network support for better coverage

The feature is rolling out starting today on Pixel 9 and newer phones that have Google Fi active on eSIM and have any non-Fi SIMs disabled.
Google Fi is bringing back multiple cell network support for better coverage
Google Fi will swap users between two 5G networks, but only if your phone is a Pixel 9 or newer.
When Google Fi first launched in 2015, users were originally able to switch between T-Mobile and Sprint’s networks. But those two networks eventually became one when T-Mobile acquired Sprint in 2020, and so the network switching stopped there. Jane Harnett, Google Fi Wireless senior product manager, told The Verge that Fi stopped offering the feature because “the wireless landscape consolidated via mergers and limited our ability to offer multiple networks within the US.” (Networking switching has continued to be available internationally.)
Now the feature is returning to the US, with Fi once again hopping between two networks. Harnett declined to share which networks Fi will be working with to make this happen. Google Fi’s FAQs say it currently provides coverage through T-Mobile’s network.

articles.title: Robô constrói estrutura no espaço sem controle humano direto pela primeira vez
articles.summary:
Um robô conseguiu montar autonomamente uma estrutura em órbita da Terra pela primeira vez na história. O experimento, financiado pela Agência de Projetos de Pesquisa Avançada de Defesa dos Estados Unidos (DARPA, na sigla em inglês) e conduzido por pesquisadores do Instituto de Tecnologia da Califórnia (Caltech), demonstrou que máquinas podem realizar trabalhos de construção no espaço com pouca intervenção humana.
Batizado de Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly (ASTRA), o projeto utilizou um equipamento robótico para montar uma antena refletora de 1,4 metro de largura. A estrutura foi construída com filme de Kapton, tubos de fibra composta e juntas de alumínio.
Segundo Sergio Pellegrino, professor de engenharia aeroespacial e civil do Caltech e líder da equipe, esta foi a primeira vez que uma estrutura foi construída autonomamente no espaço.

articles.title: Over a Dozen Organizations Hit in Qubole Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary:
A threat actor used the compromised IAM credentials for an AWS account associated with big-data platform Qubole to steal data from over a dozen organizations, cybersecurity researchers discovered.
The credentials allowed the attackers to assume IAM roles organizations had set up for Qubole’s AWS account and access their AWS environments.
Cross-account IAM roles are normal for SaaS platforms that operate within customers’ AWS environments. During onboarding, customers create a role for Qubole, and the vendor’s AWS account can assume the role when needed, typically via an External ID.
The leaked Qubole credentials allowed the threat actor to assume this role and pull data from the AWS environments of over a dozen companies.
“The doors the attacker used were old ones. Qubole roles were still in place long after companies had stopped using Qubole, and those roles could read nearly all of the data the attacker went after,” cybersecurity firm Sentra notes.
The roles stayed dormant until the campaign kicked off on October 14. They were used until October 26 to enumerate resources, collect secrets and configurations, and access data.
The attacks came from a rented OVH server and the Mullvad VPN, and none of the observed activity originated from Qubole’s network, Sentra says.
“The threat actor used role session names that followed a consistent format of the prefix quiam-, followed by a suffix describing the actions taken. This includes session names such as quiam-enum and quiam-scope-…

703 km d’autonomie, mais en ville

articles.title: Overcoming Silicon Photonics Process Control Challenges in the AI Era
articles.summary:
How connected inspection, metrology and software can help manufacturers move SiPh and CPO toward high-volume production.
More bandwidth. Lower latency. Less power consumed and less heat generated.
These are three of the challenges facing manufacturers as AI pushes electrical interconnects toward their limits. Silicon photonics (SiPh) and co-packaged optics (CPO) offer a path forward by using light to transmit data rather than relying solely on electrical signals. But realizing those benefits at production scale introduces another challenge: maintaining precise process control across the optical structures, materials and integration processes that ultimately determine device performance and yield.
At the same time, traditional copper interconnects face increasing resistance, electromigration and power challenges as semiconductor architectures scale (Figure 1). For manufacturers, the shift toward silicon photonics places greater importance on precise control of optical structures and materials.

One of the fundamental differences between conventional semiconductor manufacturing and silicon photonics is what manufacturers need to control.

articles.title: Start and Restore GPU Workloads in Seconds with NVIDIA Snapshot | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
NVIDIA Snapshot, a new open-source component of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, makes initialized GPU workloads reusable across inference replicas—speeding startup and recovery.
When inference demand spikes or a replica fails, available GPUs don’t translate immediately into serving capacity. Initializing an LLM workload—a process known as a cold start—can take minutes, delaying scaling and recovery.
Snapshot is a checkpoint and restore system for GPU workloads on Kubernetes. It captures a fully initialized workload—including CPU and GPU memory—and restores that state on compatible infrastructure, bringing inference capacity online in seconds instead of minutes. Figure 1 shows the startup sequence. Snapshot skips repeated workload initialization; infrastructure provisioning and container image loading remain outside the measured restore path.
This post explains how Snapshot checkpoints and restores GPU workloads, how platform teams can integrate it, and how restore times compare with cold starts across three inference engines.
Snapshot for AI factory operations
Originally developed for NVIDIA Dynamo inference workers, Snapshot provides checkpoint and restore capabilities that other inference engines, schedulers, controllers, and platforms can integrate.
Snapshot provides two operations for GPU Pods:
- Checkpoint: Once a workload is fully initialized, capture its CPU and GPU memory as a portable artifact.

The ICM and Web Dispatcher flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-76964 and CVE-2026-89126, are a single weakness in the SAP kernel component that receives HTTP, HTTPS, and WebSocket traffic.
According to Onapsis, which calls the security defect ICM2SHELL, the issue is related to reassembling large WebSocket messages, which may be split into fragments during a server-browser exchange and then put together by the receiver.

ICM2SHELL, the enterprise application security firm says, could allow an attacker to execute operating system commands with <sid>adm privileges.

Google has released emergency security updates to patch a new Chrome vulnerability exploited in zero-day attacks, the eighth such flaw since the start of the year.
"Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild," the company said in a Monday security advisory.
As Google explained, this flaw stems from a Use-After-Free (UAF) weakness in the XML component of the Google Chrome web browser, which occurs when the browser's XML parser processes data, deletes an object from the computer's memory, but fails to clear the pointer referencing that object.
Attackers can exploit this high-severity memory corruption vulnerability when the browser later tries to use or read that "freed" memory space to manipulate the memory layout and execute malicious code.
While Google has found evidence of attackers exploiting this zero-day bug in the wild, it has not shared additional details about these incidents.
"Access to bug details and links may be kept restricted until a majority of users are updated with a fix. We will also retain restrictions if the bug exists in a third party library that other projects similarly depend on, but haven't yet fixed," it noted.
Google has now fixed the zero-day for users in the Stable Desktop channel, with new versions rolling out to Windows, macOS (157.0.8103.50/.51), and Linux users (157.0.8103.50). articles.title: Shrinking Hybrid Bonding Pitches Push Inspection Limits
articles.summary:
Existing inspection tools struggle to capture defects, especially those hidden at the bond interface.
Key Takeaways:
Hybrid bonding represents a paradigm shift in advanced packaging, replacing 35 µm off-chip microbumps with 10 µm pitch or smaller pad-to-pad interconnects on-chip. It can be used to join silicon-to-silicon, as in DRAM-DRAM bonding in future HBM devices, or even disparate materials like GaN-on-silicon.
This elegant process, which is available on wafer-to-wafer or die-to-wafer platforms, reduces signal delay to negligible levels while enabling smaller, thinner packages with unmatched memory/processor speeds and bandwidth. It also consumes significantly less power.
Hybrid bonding’s success depends on the performance of advanced bonding equipment, as well as metrology’s ability to verify critical alignment, cleanliness, planarity, and surface properties — both before and after bonding. Solving these challenges is proving essential to realizing the vision of true 3D integration at the bonded-chip level.
But as hybrid bonding pitches continue to scale down below today’s production levels of 4 to 9 µm, some inspection and metrology methods are struggling to meet the spatial resolution and sensitivity needed to catch all relevant defect types, especially ones buried at the bond interface. Particles, voids, overlay errors, roughness, CMP defects, and warpage threaten the bond quality between chips. Even a single particle can delaminate the top wafer from the one below, …

articles.title: Agent Substrate: Advancing Kubernetes for Agents at Scale | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
AI agents spend most of their time idle, waiting on a human prompt, a tool result or a model response. Kubernetes wasn’t built for that. Running one Pod per session holds memory for sessions that aren’t doing anything, and deleting Pods between turns pays a multi-second cold start every time and loses the agent’s state. RL post-training hits the same wall.
Agent Substrate, now donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox, is an open-source, security-hardened, zero-trust runtime for sandboxed agents, engineered to safely run millions of agents and tools with 10x higher density than standard containers. It multiplexes many sessions over a small pool of worker Pods. Idle sessions are checkpointed, memory and filesystem included, and restored onto whichever worker is free when the next request arrives. As agentic infrastructure fragments into proprietary runtimes that bypass Kubernetes, NVIDIA is contributing upstream to keep this work open.
This post covers which workloads suit Agent Substrate, what is being built upstream, and how the project works with KAI Scheduler and NVIDIA Dynamo components in the DSX AI Factory Platform.
The shape of an agent workload
Traditional web services run as a relatively small number of long-lived instances. Agents follow a different pattern: they wake up and take one step, running a shell command, editing a file, calling a test suite or calling an LLM. Then they wait, sometimes for milliseconds and sometimes for minutes, before…

articles.title: Buying an EV through your ABN? Here is what the lender actually checks - Tech Guide

By Nick Lim, Founder, Switchboard Finance
A lot of business owners are now looking at an electric vehicle as their next work car. The spec sheets get all the attention: range, charging speed, the screen in the middle of the dash. The finance gets about five minutes at the end, usually at the dealer, usually under pressure.
That is backwards. The car is the easy part. Whether a lender will fund it, on what terms and against which paperwork, is where self-employed buyers get caught out. Here is how it looks from the other side of the desk.
The first thing a lender looks at is not the car. It is the business.
How long the ABN has been active matters more than most people expect. Many lenders want to see at least two years, some will go to one, and a handful will go lower with a bigger deposit or a stronger file. GST registration matters too, partly because it signals turnover and partly because it affects how the deal can be structured.
Then comes income. A salaried employee hands over two payslips and is done. A sole trader or company director is asked for tax returns, financial statements and sometimes an accountant’s letter. If the latest return is late, shows a loss because of a one-off write-off, or simply does not reflect how the business is trading now, that is where applications stall.

articles.title: Running AV Reasoning Models Within Onboard Compute and Latency Limits | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Autonomous vehicle (AV) developers need reasoning models that can operate within the compute and latency constraints of an onboard system. Larger models provide a foundation for developing these capabilities, but moving them into a vehicle requires additional work to reduce model size, preserve useful reasoning, and validate performance on the target hardware.
NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Edge addresses this need with an adaptive reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) model designed for real-time operation on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor. Built on the 2B Nemotron-based reasoning backbone of NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge and paired with a diffusion action expert, it leverages surround-camera observations, temporal context, and navigation inputs to generate Chain-of-Causation (CoC) reasoning and future driving trajectories. It reasons adaptively, generating reasoning only when needed, reducing unnecessary token generation and conserving inference compute during routine driving.
Alpamayo 2 Edge is post-trained with closed-loop reinforcement learning (RL) in NVIDIA AlpaGym, improving closed-loop driving performance by 48.9% on top of the best-performing checkpoint without closed-loop RL. Together, these capabilities give developers a strong, edge-ready foundation for bringing reasoning-based driving into an onboard stack.

articles.title: L'Europe s'attaque à l'algorithme de TikTok : votre fil « Pour toi » pourrait changer radicalement
articles.summary:
La Commission européenne a adressé ses conclusions préliminaires à TikTok le 6 novembre : le fil « Pour toi » violerait le règlement sur les services numériques, le fameux DSA. En cause, des « terriers de lapin » algorithmiques qui aspirent le spectateur de vidéo en vidéo, parfois vers des contenus dangereux pour sa santé mentale. Pour la plateforme, l’accrochage avec Bruxelles est déjà le troisième de l’année.
Les reproches de Bruxelles à la mécanique du « Pour toi »
Le grief central vise la matière première des recommandations : le temps passé sur chaque vidéo. En s’appuyant sur ce signal passif, le système déduirait les fragilités du moment mieux que l’utilisateur ne les formulerait lui-même, puis le ramènerait sans cesse vers les mêmes contenus. Les enquêteurs décrivent des spirales nourries de vidéos sur la perte de poids ou le mal-être, « dont il est difficile de s’échapper », avertit Henna Virkkunen, la commissaire européenne à la souveraineté technologique.
Le bouton « Pas intéressé » ne pèserait presque rien face à ce signal, et les réglages qui permettent de reprendre la main restent, aux yeux de l’exécutif, trop difficiles d’accès. Bruxelles réclame donc trois corrections : cesser de bâtir les recommandations sur le temps de visionnage, donner un vrai poids aux préférences déclarées, et rendre les garde-fous accessibles sans expédition dans les menus.

articles.title: Turla hackers use new Cereal malware to spy on govt Exchange servers

The Russian state-backed threat group Turla has been using a new malicious toolset called 'Cereal' to intercept emails on Microsoft Exchange servers at government organizations.
Researchers at cybersecurity company ESET documented the attacks in late 2025, initially finding modular .NET malware for Microsoft Exchange at a government body in Kazakhstan.
A month later, ESET found the same toolset at a government agency in Romania, where it selectively gathered email correspondence with representatives of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and the European Union (EU).
"After fine-tuning our detections, we found the same toolset at a governmental organization in Romania - compromised on December 23rd, 2025," the researchers say in a report today.
Turla, also known as Snake, Secret Blizzard, and Waterbug, is a cyber-espionage group active for more than two decades and linked to Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB).
In the campaign analyzed by ESET, the hackers use the Cereal toolset, and specifically a component in the kit named CerealBox, to inject into Exchange’s EdgeTransport.exe process and hijack existing transport agents’ handlers.
The malware executes commands in memory and can inspect email content without registering a new transport agent or interrupting normal email delivery in the Exchange server.

articles.title: „Niemand will diese Arbeit machen“: Roboter übernimmt das Putzen deiner Wohnung – was dabei schief geht
articles.summary:
Ich habe einen humanoiden Roboter meine Wohnung putzen lassen – was dabei schief ging
Ich gehöre nicht zu den Menschen, die eine Reinigungskraft beschäftigen. Ich bin zu geizig, und irgendwie macht es mir auch Spaß, einen Podcast anzumachen und mich mit einem Wunder-Reinigungsschwamm an meiner Badewanne auszutoben. Aber als ich auf X einen Beitrag über einen neuen Reinigungsdienst mit humanoiden Robotern in San Francisco sah, habe ich mich sofort auf die Warteliste setzen lassen. Ich wollte, dass sich meine Wohnung wie bei der 1960er-Jahre-Cartoonserie „Die Jetsons“ anfühlt, und sei es auch nur für eine Stunde.
Außerdem war ich aus journalistischem Interesse motiviert. Um ein authentisches Erlebnis zu gewährleisten, habe ich Tau Robotics, dem Startup hinter dem X-Beitrag, nicht gesagt, dass ich Journalistin bin – obwohl ich meinen richtigen Namen angegeben habe, sodass es möglich ist, dass jemand mich ausfindig gemacht hat.
Für 30 US-Dollar kommt ein humanoider Roboter in meine Wohnung zum Putzen

Friedman, who helped drive early government and industry work around SBOM, offered perhaps the simplest explanation for why the concept matters.

articles.title: Effect 4.0 Ships: Dependency-Free Rewrite with 5x Smaller Bundles and Long-Term Support
articles.summary:
Effect, the TypeScript framework for building production-grade applications with typed errors, structured concurrency and dependency injection, has released Effect 4.0. Published on 30 September 2026, it is the first stable version of a line that spent eight months in beta and six weeks in release candidate.
Effect 4.0 is a from-scratch rewrite of the fiber runtime, aimed at smaller bundles, lower memory use and higher throughput. The team's own figures put a minimal program using Effect, Stream and Schema at 7.1 kB against 35.6 kB in 3.x, a 5x reduction. The heap used by 50,000 fibers drops from 157.5 MB to 21.8 MB, an 86% cut, and concurrent task throughput moves from 0.71 million to 4.57 million tasks per second, roughly 6.4x. The numbers are medians of nine fresh-process runs on identical source, and as noted by stork.ai, have not been independently reproduced.
Alongside the rewrite, the ecosystem has been consolidated. Core modules from @effect/platform, @effect/rpc and @effect/cluster now live inside the main effect package, every @effect/* package shares a single version, and the core ships with zero runtime dependencies after the final removal of pg (replaced by a native PgProtocol client) and MessagePack.
With 4.0, the team has introduced a long-term support policy. Effect 4.x receives bug fixes until September 2029, or one year after 5.0 ships, whichever is later. Security fixes run until September 2029 or two years after 5.0, again whichever is later.

articles.title: SAP patches ICM2SHELL and PROXYGATE maximum severity flaws
articles.summary:
SAP patched 35 vulnerabilities in its November 2026 security updates, including four maximum-severity issues affecting its NetWeaver, Web Dispatcher, and Gateway software.
The company addressed memory corruption (CVE-2026-76964) and missing authentication (CVE-2026-120017) flaws in the NetWeaver Application Server ABAP's Internet Communication Manager and SAML2 Service Provider components.
NetWeaver is the core app platform that underpins SAP's business software and handles application integration, authentication, user management, and data processing.
The other two maximum severity vulnerabilities stem from a broken access control weakness (CVE-2026-89103) in SAP Gateway and a memory corruption issue (CVE-2026-89126) in SAP Web Dispatcher.
Gateway is a core framework that enables external apps to securely connect to SAP backend systems, while Web Dispatcher (deployed in almost every enterprise SAP environment) is a specialized component that acts as a load balancer and reverse proxy for web requests entering an SAP system architecture.
Cybersecurity firm Onapsis, which found and reported three of these security issues, collectively tracks CVE-2026-76964 and CVE-2026-89126 as ICM2SHELL and the CVE-2026-89103 pre-auth remote code execution vulnerability as PROXYGATE.

articles.title: Adobe Patches 110 Vulnerabilities Across 9 Products
articles.summary:
Adobe’s November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates fix roughly 110 vulnerabilities across nine products.
New patches are available for Adobe Experience Manager (AEM), Audition, After Effects, Connect, Content Credentials SDK, Dimension, Media Encoder, Photoshop, and Premiere.
Critical-severity issues have been patched in Adobe Connect and AEM, including six Connect flaws with a CVSS score of 10.
The critical flaws include SSRF, path traversal, incorrect authorization, CRLF injection, XXE, code injection, SQL injection, and XSS issues. They can be exploited for privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution.
A total of 38 vulnerabilities have been resolved in AEM and Connect, including high- and medium-severity issues whose exploitation can lead to privilege escalation, file system read, memory exposure, arbitrary code execution, and bypassing security features.
High-severity bugs have been fixed in After Effects, Media Encoder, Premiere, Dimension, Audition, and Photoshop.
The Content Credentials Rust SDK (and the C2PA Tool) received patches for roughly a dozen low- and medium-severity issues.
Adobe says it’s not aware of attacks exploiting the newly patched vulnerabilities.
The Connect and AEM patches have a priority rating of 2; the rest are rated 3, which means they are unlikely to be exploited in the wild.

articles.title: Iomega Zip Drive: Elite Floppy Disks Before USB Sticks
articles.summary:
These days, backing up your files or sharing them with others is a walk in the park. For most purposes, a cloud service will do. For sensitive or very large files, you can plug an external drive into a USB port. In the 1990s, however, things were more complicated.
Back then, most homes weren't connected to the internet, and the few that were paid by the minute to transfer a few kilobytes per second. Flash memory was reserved for premium digital cameras and, in tiny quantities, console memory cards.
IBM had standardized the 1.44MB format for lightweight, slow-spinning floppy disks with the PS/2 series. That was enough for documents and spreadsheets, but became a problem for larger file types, such as uncompressed graphical work. Software came on CDs (or many, many floppies), but CD recorders weren't affordable yet.
If you wanted to share large files between computers that weren't in the same room, your most convenient option might have been to unscrew your hard disk (we remember doing this on a very regular basis actually), a device built for spinning fast rather than traveling, and install it in the other computer.
Image credit: LGR
Years before USB drives and broadband internet, the Iomega Zip drive packed 100MB of storage into a 3.5 inch format that fit in your pocket. It let you carry all your files anywhere and gave the first generation of independent graphic designers the freedom to work on the move.

Recovering from ransomware is only part of the job. Clients also need to know what happened, what recovery involved and what it cost them. articles.title: Starlink Mini 2 adds a swappable battery
articles.summary:
SpaceX announced a new version of its all-in-one satellite internet terminal that integrates a dish, Wi-Fi router, and now a battery into a single device about the size of a laptop. According to some users on X who shared screenshots of invitations to order Starlink Mini 2, the dish is priced at $999, which includes a full year of Roam Unlimited service that SpaceX values at $2,100.
Starlink Mini 2 adds a swappable battery
The all-in-one satellite dish can now operate for over four hours without an external power source.
The Starlink Mini 2 will run for up to 4.5 hours on a full charge, SpaceX claims, but that can be expanded by hot-swapping in additional batteries that will be sold separately, or by connecting the dish to a 60W power source over USB-C.
Despite the addition of an integrated battery, the Starlink Mini 2 dish is thinner than the original Mini. SpaceX has managed to slim it down to 23.1mm thick, while the previous version of the Mini was 38.5mm. The Starlink Mini 2 is slightly heavier at around 3.5 pounds as a result of the added battery weight, but carries forward an IP67 dust- and waterproof rating so it’s still safe to use outdoors.
Preorders are now open “by invitation for select US customers,” according to the Starlink website, but “coming soon” to more customers and countries.

articles.title: Exploited Outlook Zero-Day Among 1,094 Flaws Patched by Microsoft
articles.summary:
Microsoft’s November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates fix 1,094 vulnerabilities across its products, including an Outlook bug that the company says has been exploited.
The zero-day, tracked as CVE-2026-124194, has been classified as a spoofing flaw and stems from Outlook not alerting users before a potentially dangerous action takes place.
Microsoft has assigned it a severity rating of ‘moderate’ and a CVSS score of 6.5. The company’s advisory provides no information about the observed attacks.
For an attack to work, the victim needs to be tricked into opening a malicious file, according to Microsoft.
“An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted message file and convince a user to open it in an affected version of Microsoft Outlook. Opening the file could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information that could be used to impersonate the user,” the tech giant said.
The flaw cannot be triggered through the Preview Pane, Microsoft said. It also clarified, “This vulnerability discloses a user’s NTLMv2 hash to the attacker who could use this to authenticate as the user.”
The vulnerability was not publicly disclosed before the fix became available. Affected products include Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, Office LTSC 2021, and Office LTSC 2024.

articles.title: We Source Chips Others Cannot Secure, 2026 - EE Times
articles.summary:
In 2026, the global electronic components supply chain continues to navigate choppy waters.
For buyers and engineers across Europe and the US, the real headache is never simply “can I get the part?” It is four problems hitting at once: unstable lead times, volatile pricing, counterfeit and refurbished parts flooding the market, and critical part numbers that can go out of stock without warning. When a single chip’s lead time stretches from 8 weeks to 20, a production line grinds to a halt. When a batch of parts of unknown origin slips into a BOM, the cost isn’t just money — it’s delivery credibility and customer trust.
Over the past three years, the industry has been through a full downcycle. Demand contracted, inventory piled up, and prices fell. Many buyers thought they could finally breathe easy. But the reality is the opposite: the colder the market, the more traps appear in the supply chain. Mainstream part numbers are readily available with short lead times — but the moment you hit an allocation-constrained, end-of-life, or hard-to-find part, lead times can jump from weeks to months overnight. Meanwhile, unscrupulous dealers, driven by high margins, continue to supply substandard products — and the tougher the market, the more willing some are to cut corners. Prices swing, quotes are hard to hold, and buyers are squeezed between suppliers and internal cost targets. The metals industry has experienced transformational moments before: the Bessemer process, flash smelting, electric arc furnaces, and modern continuous casting all changed what was possible.
Yet, for more than a century, most extraction processes rely on techniques and pathways that would be familiar to metallurgists from generations ago. Processes have become larger and control systems smarter, but the fundamental science behind separating metals from ores has changed less than many realize.

articles.title: LLM Reliability Layers Under Test: Accuracy, Yield, and the Limits of Verification
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Reliability layers sorted answers by trustworthiness but corrected almost none; yield, right answers over all records, exposes what accuracy hides.
- Deterministic code can prove an answer wrong, never right: it catches nonexistent codes and spans missing from the post, but plausible answers still need a model or a person.
- Recognition beats generation: recalling SNOMED codes from memory, the model invented 13 to 18 percent that don’t exist; picking from a menu, it scored ten times higher.
- Determinism held: four of five model families reproduced their output exactly at temperature zero; the fifth agreed on 70 percent of mentions across three runs.
- Detection sets a hard ceiling: no layer recovers a mention the extractor missed, so the largest gains came from matching the corpus’s annotation conventions, not domain-adapted models.
The theory: More layers should mean more accuracy
Clinical notes, incident reports, support tickets, and forum posts are prose, and a language model can read them. What it produces is not dependable. articles.title: Claude Code's "don't ask again" button is leaking passwords and API keys to public GitHub repos
articles.summary:
Facepalm: A feature in Claude Code meant to save developers a few clicks is exposing database passwords, API tokens and private keys in public GitHub repositories. When a developer tells Anthropic's coding agent to stop asking for permission to run a shell command, the agent saves the exact command, along with any credentials inside it, to a settings file in the project folder. Researchers at security firm Apiiro found that file in more than 100,000 public repositories, and about 1,100 of them contained secrets.
Claude Code asks for approval before it runs shell commands on a developer's machine. One of the options is "Yes, and don't ask again." Choosing it creates an allow rule in a file called .claude/settings.local.json. Sometimes the rule is a general pattern, but often it's the full command, stored word for word. If that command included a password, a token or a root login, the credential now sits in plain text in a JSON file inside the project directory.
Anthropic's documentation says Claude Code adds an entry for this file to the developer's global Git ignore configuration. That normally keeps Git from tracking it. But a global ignore list lives in the developer's own Git configuration, not in the repository. If the repository is cloned to a different machine, or if a folder that already holds the file is turned into a repository later, that protection may not be in place. Apiiro also reports that Claude Code often commits changes to the settings file on its own, witho…

articles.title: FDA warns GLP-1 drugs may pose risk of rare condition that causes vision loss
articles.summary:
The Food and Drug Administration is warning that popular obesity drugs—including Ozempic, Wegovy, Zepbound, and Mounjaro—may carry a “potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition that can lead to permanent vision loss.
In a drug safety communication Monday, the FDA said it will now require makers of GLP-1 receptor agonist drugs to add a warning about that risk on their drug labels. The specific eye condition it warns of is called non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy or NAION. The condition is caused by restricted blood flow to the optic nerve, which leads to swelling and cell death and ultimately damages the nerve, causing abrupt vision loss that can often be permanent.
It’s unknown how GLP-1 drugs may cause NAION. The condition is rare overall, occurring in somewhere between two and 10 people in 100,000 in the general population, according to the American Academy of Ophthalmology. These small numbers have made it more difficult to determine with certainty if there is a connection. Further complicating the potential link is the fact that the risk factors for developing NAION are common among patients taking GLP-1 drugs. The risk factors include diabetes, cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, metabolic syndrome, and obstructive sleep apnea.
Mixed data
The first study suggesting a link between GLP-1 drugs and NAION came in 2024 from Harvard University researchers. Their study, published in JAMA Ophthalmology, looked at 710 patients with…

Si el proyecto se clona en otro equipo, si una carpeta se convierte en proyecto más tarde o si el archivo ya estaba registrado, la exclusión no actúa y el archivo se sube con el resto del código. A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited in attacks that could grant administrator privileges and allow takeover of XCP-ng virtualization hosts.
Xen Orchestra is a web-based management platform developed by French software company Vates, used to manage XCP-ng virtualization environments, including virtual machines, hosts, and pools.
The vulnerability, tracked as VSA-2026-062, affects Xen Orchestra and the Xen Orchestra Appliance (XOA) and allows remote attackers with network access to the management interface to bypass authentication using a specially crafted cookie. A CVE identifier and CVSS score have not been assigned yet.
According to a Vates security advisory, the flaw stems from how Xen Orchestra processes authentication tokens sent through REST API requests.
The flaw stems from how Xen Orchestra processes authentication cookies.
By sending a specially crafted cookie (authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D) containing an empty JSON object ({}), attackers can trick the platform into retrieving an existing authentication token and logging them in as its owner, without requiring actual credentials.
Once authenticated, attackers can retrieve "reusable login token IDs" through the /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens REST API endpoint, which can be used for further access.

articles.title: Test Struggles To Keep Pace With AI
articles.summary:
Rapidly changing workloads, more test insertions, and fragmented data complicate chip testing.
Key Takeaways:
The rapid pace of change in AI models and approaches is creating confusion over what to test, when to test it, and what to monitor once chips are in the field.
Until recently, test targets and the timing for test insertions generally were determined by fab processes and the laws of physics, and the results of those tests were deterministic and quantifiable. But starting with the rollout of generative AI and the ensuing explosion of data centers, the gap has widened between the rollout of new algorithms and use models and the time it takes to deploy a chip in the field.
An increasing number of high-performance processors used in data centers, and many at the edge, are multi-die assemblies. The chips are more complex and take longer to design, manufacture, package, and assemble, and the workloads for which they are designed often change by the time those chips leave final test. Along the way, there are more test insertions along the way, each of which generates more data.
The tests are more complex and varied, as well. In addition to electrical tests, these chips need to be analyzed for mechanical integrity. AI workloads can stress one part of a multi-die assembly more than others, and they can change quickly as algorithms and use cases evolve. articles.title: Pinterest and Intel Take Open-Source Profiling to Internet Scale

Pinterest has partnered with Intel to extend gProfiler, an open-source continuous profiler that provides production performance visibility across an internet-scale fleet of infrastructure.
Pinterest claims it operates hundreds of thousands of instances supporting 640 million monthly active users, with services written in Java, Python, C++, Go, and Node.js. At that scale, even a small efficiency improvement can have significant infrastructure and cost implications. The challenge was that engineers were using separate tools such as perf, async-profiler, and py-spy, producing fragmented profiles that were difficult to correlate across languages and machines.
Rather than building another proprietary profiling platform, Pinterest worked with Intel to extend gProfiler and contribute those capabilities back to the open-source project. The collaboration adds dynamic profiling, hardware-level telemetry, wall-time profiling, and performance-counter flame graphs, while also hardening the system for large production fleets.
gProfiler acts as an orchestration layer over several existing profilers. It combines system-wide perf data with runtime-specific tools such as async-profiler for Java and eBPF-based profiling for Python, producing a unified flame graph across the processes running on a host.

articles.title: Google Finds that Technical Debt Can Derail Coding Agents Through "Agent Distraction"
articles.summary:
In a recent article, Google senior staff software engineer Sam Saccone and senior staff data scientist Madhuri Garikapati highlighted the cost of agent distraction, where AI coding agents get derailed by stale technical debt, such as old TODO comments, obsolete bug references, and outdated specs, leading them to embark on unrequested "side-quests".
Obsolete specs, long resolved bugs, and lagging documentation no longer rest in long forgotten corners of the codebase, but rather are unintentionally ingested as context indirecting and misdirecting the next wave of coders - the agents.
According to the authors, at best, agent distraction increases token consumption and execution time; at worst, it can lead agents to "incorrect logic and decisions". To investigate this impact, they focused on TODO(bug/...) comments, which, as they note, "tend to be left behind long after the underlying bug is resolved or abandoned".
By cross-referencing every TODO an agent encounters against the TODO's bug status and the user's prompt, we can automatically separate valid work from wasted detours at scale.
Using distributed traces from thousands of engineers and hundreds of millions of agent steps, Google found that approximately 13% of sessions exposed agents to inline TODO/FIXME references, leading agents to take action targeting the reference bug in 6% of those cases. In most cases, the prompt did not even mention the referenced bug. Furthermore, in 41% of these unprompted detours, the agent wor…

That's enough gas-fired equipment to produce 1.7 gigawatts of power.
The deal makes it the largest known purchase of power-generation gear by any AI lab, according to the Financial Times. Anthropic signed the agreement back in late September with San Antonio-based supplier OnePWR Solutions. OnePWR had ordered the generators from Caterpillar about two years earlier, but it was still short on the financing needed to complete the purchase.

The campaign ran between October 14 and 26, and affected tens of companies whose AWS environments had IAM roles configured to trust an AWS account associated with Qubole.
Qubole is an enterprise cloud data processing and analytics platform that helps companies manage large datasets and run machine learning workloads. It also offers AWS integration to allow computing resource management.
Companies can grant third-party providers such as Qubole access to their AWS resources by creating cross-account IAM roles. Trust policies determine which external AWS accounts can take these roles, and permissions are set to define the resources and actions allowed.
Researchers at cloud security company Wiz explain that external providers use AWS’s STS AssumeRole API to obtain temporary credentials for accessing customers' resources in the cloud.
Wiz started to investigate the attack after data security and governance company Sentra shared information about suspicious activity observed in some of its customers' environments. The investigation also included cybersecurity company Mandiant.

Los bancos y los inversores que financiaron la expansión de la inteligencia artificial empezaron a vender o a rechazar deuda ligada a los centros de datos. El medio Semafor informó que hay carteras de préstamos ofrecidas con fuertes descuentos y que los créditos para comprar chips son los más castigados.

AI made coding faster. It didn’t make software simpler
Coding is faster, but the winners will be those that create more value from it
For years, the software industry operated under one core assumption: writing code was the primary bottleneck in software development. As a result, companies poured enormous resources into hiring developers, refining development processes, and building tools that could shorten the journey from idea to product.
Then generative AI arrived.
For the first time, the industry gained a technology capable of solving the very problem it had spent decades trying to overcome. The ability to write code – once the industry’s most constrained resource – is now faster, more accessible, and dramatically more efficient.
But if our ability to generate code has increased so dramatically, why aren’t software organizations moving at the same pace?
General Manager of CX Engineering at NiCE.
AI-enabled development offers a more nuanced story. AI coding agents can handle work that previously required additional engineering capacity, from creating the foundations of an application to generating tests and accelerating implementation. A group of two or three people can try out an idea that might once have required a much larger team, more specialized skills, and considerably more time.
But speed is only part of the story. The more important change is that AI expands the ambition of each team.

articles.title: Carbon emissions are down this year—but that probably won’t last
articles.summary:
Evaluating the annual global temperatures each year requires context. There is a fair amount of natural variability from one year to the next, so it’s important to focus on the trend over time. Famously, global warming did not end in 1998, as some claimed a couple of decades ago—we just had a run of La-Niña-dominated years after a very strong El Niño.
Annual greenhouse gas emissions are much less variable, having increased fairly steadily, but many complicating factors can still muddy the picture. Sometimes those factors conspire to throw a year off the trend. It looks like 2026 will be one of those years.
A new analysis led by Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia estimates that fossil fuel emissions have fallen about 0.4 percent from last year. This probably isn’t a peak that symbolizes heartening progress on climate change, though; the researchers think it’s a short-term dip driven by the war in Iran and its effect on oil prices.
Shifting percentages
This team works on the Global Carbon Project, which compiles stats on fossil fuel use and things like deforestation to track carbon emissions globally and by country. In this case, they looked at the stats and tried to pull out key underlying trends that show us what to expect over the next couple of years.

Since Valve announced its Steam Deck Verified program in 2021, players have found that a game’s “Verified” status doesn’t always match how well it actually runs on the handheld. Now, new Steam Deck frame rate data being shared by Valve itself can help players dig deeper into the performance they can expect from many Steam Deck games.

Valve acknowledges that players enabling VSync or frame rate limits can bias the collected data somewhat and that the measurements don’t account for custom in-game settings that Steam Deck users may tinker with to get a game running. Teleport makes Beams generally available to bring AI agents into production
Infrastructure identity company Teleport today made Teleport Beams, its runtime for artificial intelligence agents that work on production infrastructure, generally available.
Beams goes after what Teleport sees as the main reason agents have stayed out of production so far. Most enterprises have not plugged agents into those systems at all, according to Ev Kontsevoy, Teleport’s co-founder and chief executive. He blamed gaps such as delegated identity and an audit trail that follows an agent from intent to action.
Sandboxes, the tool many teams reach for now, mostly isolate the agent in a virtual machine and handle its credentials. “When the cost of an error is high, traditional sandboxes don’t cut it,” Kontsevoy said ahead of the announcement.
Teleport calls each individual runtime a Beam, and every agent gets its own. A Beam carries a delegated identity inherited from the user or agent that launched it, while the agent inside starts with no standing privileges. Work begins with a proposed execution plan. That plan can be revised by a person or by a large language model acting as judge before a separate Beam runs it with only the approved roles. Reviewers then see new requests only for steps outside the plan.

articles.title: AMD's RDNA 5 Inches Closer as GFX13 Support Lands in Linux Driver Patches
articles.summary:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
AMD's RDNA 5 Inches Closer as GFX13 Support Lands in Linux Driver Patches
AMD has begun integrating its next-generation graphics IP into the Linux kernel, releasing a series of eight patches that add GFX13 support to the open-source AMDGPU driver. These patches, submitted to the mailing list on November 9 by AMDGPU maintainer Alex Deucher, contain over 12,600 lines of code, excluding the typically large header files. GFX13 is anticipated to be the graphics core for RDNA 5, although AMD has not officially confirmed this connection. However, since GFX12 has been linked to RDNA 4, it is assumed that GFX13 is the correct codename for RDNA 5.
The patches introduce version 13 of three IP blocks: the "graphics" GFX block itself, the MicroEngine Scheduler (MES), and the IMU. On the compute side, the AMDKFD driver gains initial GC 13 support, a CWSR trap handler for saving and restoring compute wave state, and a temporary change that disables queue reset in the topology. The final patch enables the MGCG, CGCG, and CGLS clock gating features, which reduce power consumption when parts of the GPU are idle. Interestingly, the series mentions two specific targets, GFX 13.0.1 and GFX 13.0.4, indicating that AMD is preparing at least two graphics IP configurations. These version numbers do not correspond to any specific GPU models, so it is unclear which products they relate to. RDNA 5 is expected to be a significant advancement over RDNA 4, necessitating numerous…

articles.title: Your meditation headband may be feeding your brainwaves to an AI model

In brief: Companies that direct users' texts, emails, art, online behavior, and other work or private data to advertisers and AI training models have long been under scrutiny. However, a recent report highlights how similar practices in the brain-computer industry have largely flown under the radar. Some experts say consumer brain scanners can't collect much data, but others worry about what might happen if advertisers and AI companies can access users' brain activity.
A recent report from the journal Science outlines the relationship between the electroencephalography (EEG) industry and AI. It found that some companies selling brain-tracking devices aren't entirely forthcoming about where users' brain-signal data ends up.
InteraXon's Muse brain-sensing headband is a leading example. The $475 device tracks and charts users' brainwaves to help improve sleep and focus. But the company didn't inform users that it was using data from some headbands, supposedly anonymized, to train its AI model of the brain until after Science notified them.
Science also examined the privacy policies of dozens of other consumer-facing EEG companies and found that around one-third didn't clearly explain how they handle user brainwave data. Of those companies, 11 had policies that mentioned only how users interact with their websites, and four had no privacy policies at all.
A relatively little-known industry has been exploring EEG devices since long before the AI boom. InteraXon first unveiled what…

articles.title: Pulsar “Sí, y no vuelvas a preguntar” en Claude Code parecía inofensivo. Ha acabado filtrando miles de contraseñas en GitHub

"Sí a todo" y que pase lo que tenga que pasar.
En el caso de Claude Code, marcar la casilla de no volver a preguntar implicaba que el comando aprobado se guardaba tal cual, con las contraseñas que llevase escritas, en un archivo que podía acabar en el código elaborado por la IA. Rapidus Could Miss 2 nm Mass Production Timeline Amid SRAM Issues
Japanese semiconductor maker Rapidus might miss the planned timeline for its 2 nm node production, as the company is reportedly struggling with its initial attempts at risk production and trial runs. According to a report by the Japan Times, 2 nm volume production at Rapidus facilities will likely be delayed by a few months due to difficulties in 2 nm production, specifically with SRAM. SRAM consists of tiny bitcells that serve as the foundational building blocks for designs operating on one node, and without functional SRAM, it is simply impossible to achieve normal volume production.
There are reportedly other problems, including dust and particle control, which are impacting Rapidus cleanrooms—where the actual silicon is manufactured—to a point where production may be jeopardized altogether. articles.title: Google Fi adds support for a second 5G network, won't say which one
articles.summary:
Google has announced a “super network” upgrade for its Fi cell service. For the past few years, Google Fi has operated exclusively on the T-Mobile network, but now it’s adding support for a second 5G network. Oddly, Google refuses to say which one.
Google’s MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) launched in 2015 as Project Fi with support for both T-Mobile and Sprint service. The service initially only worked on Google’s Nexus phones, which would switch between networks based on signal strength. After T-Mobile absorbed Sprint, Fi switched to being a single-network service in the US while continuing to hop between networks for international travel.
With the super network, Google Fi is again a dual-carrier service stateside. Phones connected to Fi will be able to hop between T-Mobile 5G and a different 5G network to provide the best possible connectivity. Google’s blog post announcing the change conspicuously doesn’t mention either network, saying only that it supports “two of America’s best 5G cellular networks.”
We know one of them is T-Mobile, and the other must be either AT&T or Verizon. When reached for comment, a Google spokesperson declined to name the second network, which is odd. Looking at the Fi coverage map, my best guess for the super network partner is Verizon. The shape of unserved regions is a closer match than AT&T, but carriers do tend to fudge the fine details of these maps.

Ihren Simulationen zufolge liegt die Temperatur selbst an den kältesten Stellen im Durchschnitt eines Sonnenumlaufs bei mindestens 212 Kelvin, was minus 61 Grad Celsius entspricht, während Wassereis im Vakuum selbst unter einer schützenden Gesteinsschicht nur unterhalb von 145 Kelvin beziehungsweise minus 128 Grad Celsius über längere Zeiträume stabil bleibt.

El 11 de noviembre de 2025, una tormenta solar desató el mayor pulso de radiación atmosférica en casi dos décadas, lo que activó un inédito despliegue científico para medir su impacto en el hemisferio norte. El fenómeno cósmico, originado por una potente erupción de clase X5, provocó un flujo repentino de partículas que penetraron la atmósfera hasta alcanzar la superficie terrestre.
Durante años, la seguridad de las rutas aéreas y los dispositivos electrónicos frente a estas tempestades dependió de simulaciones teóricas por computadora. La falta de registros físicos en tiempo real impedía calibrar la verdadera intensidad de estas dosis, una ausencia que dejaba abierta una incógnita crítica sobre los riesgos sanitarios para tripulaciones frecuentes y la vulnerabilidad técnica de los instrumentos de vuelo.
Para resolver esa falta de datos directos, la Universidad de Surrey coordinó una red internacional de sensores distribuidos desde la superficie hasta globos en la estratosfera para evaluar la radiación descendente, según reveló un estudio en Space Weather. El hallazgo comprobó que los niveles de exposición superaron los límites de seguridad en rutas privadas y supersónicas sin que los protocolos habituales emitieran ninguna advertencia operativa.

Data teams setting up PuppyGraph 1.0 start from a schema that an AI-assisted tool drafts out of their existing tables. Once they have approved it, users can put questions to the graph in plain English.

Google’s answer to Apple’s AirTag, the Google Pixel Tag, goes on sale starting Tuesday, allowing Android users to track items like their keys, wallet, or bag using their smartphone’s built-in Find Hub.
First announced in August, the $29.99 device takes cues from the AirTag and other lost-item finders by offering connectivity via Bluetooth and ultra-wideband for precision finding. articles.summary:
Elon Musk’s Terafab targets 1 million wafers a month after 2032 — planned 700,000 monthly memory wafers could rival Samsung’s entire estimated DRAM production capacity
Terafab’s procurement team reportedly has already been to Japan, asking some toolmakers to deliver within months.
Elon Musk’s Terafab, a joint venture of Tesla and SpaceX, has informally told equipment makers it is seeking to produce 1 million wafers per month after 2032, according to Financial News. About 70% of this output, or 700,000 wafers, is planned to go to memory, with more than 300,000 going to logic chips. Terafab’s procurement team has already visited Japan to ask some local toolmakers for delivery within months. The memory allotment would rival Samsung’s estimated DRAM production capacity if it were all of that type.
Samsung’s DRAM capacity was estimated last year at 650,000–700,000 wafers a month, while SK hynix is reportedly at about 550,000, with about 1 million a goal by 2030. The comparison has to be taken in context, as Terafab’s 700,000 measures all of its expected memory output, which could be NAND or DRAM, while the Samsung and SK hynix figures measure only DRAM. As it is, the memory portion alone would be 3.5 times the reported 200,000 at SK hynix’s Wuxi fab in China.

articles.title: AEMET ha confirmado que Charles superará el umbral de ciclogénesis explosiva y el problema no es la lluvia: son las rachas de viento de hasta 140 km/h
articles.summary:
A las 05:40 del 28 de enero de 2026, una estación meteorológica situada en un parque eólico al suroeste de Coimbra marcó una racha de 208,8 km/h. Es, hasta la fecha, la velocidad más alta que se ha registrado en el interior de la península Ibérica. Pues bien, si todo sale como dicen algunos modelos, ese récord podría estar a punto de romperse.
Por si acaso, Portugal ya ha ordenado cerrar sus colegios este miércoles y muchas escuelas a este lado de la raya han seguido el mismo camino. El motivo no es Charles, como tampoco lo fue Kristin aquel 28 de enero: es un fenómeno conocido como 'chorro en aguijón'. El problema es que una ciclogénesis explosiva como la que tenemos encima es un terreno abonado para que se repita.
Y, aunque no lo haga, rachas de 140 km/h en superficie sobre la Península es algo muy poco habitual (más allá de cabos y cumbres). Y extremadamente peligroso.
Lo que está confirmado. AEMET explicaba este martes que la presión en el centro de Charles va a caer 19 hectopascales en 24 horas. A las latitudes por las que se mueve (entre 35 y 38° N) el listón de la ciclogénesis explosiva está entre 15,9 y 17,1 hPa; así que lo salta. No de forma extremadamente llamativa, pero lo hace.
La agencia habla de "vientos huracanados" y, pese a las apariencias, hablamos de rachas de viento. No de vientos sostenidos. Es justo lo que hablaba sobre el 'chorro en aguijón': una corriente de aire que cae desde la parte alta de la borrasca hasta el suelo generando periodos de viento de …

Nesbitt-Smith usó los modelos Opus y Sonnet de Claude, de Anthropic, en una computadora portátil y con versiones disponibles para cualquier usuario. El caso más grave fue el de la Inspección de Planificación (Planning Inspectorate), el organismo que tramita asuntos de uso del suelo en Inglaterra. Había subido por error a GitHub, un sitio donde se comparte código, una credencial de acceso, y no la eliminó por completo.
Según el investigador, la credencial no parecía vencer y daba un acceso muy amplio, lo que la hacía “particularmente peligrosa”. Con ella se habría podido leer y modificar todos los sitios de SharePoint y las cuentas privadas de OneDrive de los empleados (servicios de Microsoft para guardar archivos), incluidos registros de recursos humanos.

Cyber insurance provider Cowbell Cyber Inc. today unveiled Cowbell AI Liability Insurance, a standalone policy for U.S. small and midsized businesses that covers losses caused by the artificial intelligence agents they deploy.
The new policy is meant to deal with a problem that arises when businesses let agents move money or change customer records with nobody signing off first. Coverage hinges on a trigger the company calls an “AI Incident.” The definition takes in model drift and attacks that manipulate an agent, not just software acting without approval.
Cowbell describes an accounts payable agent misreading approval statuses and paying a supplier twice with no human check. Part of that money disappears when the supplier goes into liquidation.
Unrecovered funds like those can be covered, and the policy also pays to investigate what happened and take the agent offline. Inaccurate or unsafe output can be corrected or withdrawn at the insurer’s expense, with recipients notified.
Usage charges an agent racks up without authorization are covered too, such as when a loop goes unchecked. Cowbell also covers LLMjacking, where an outsider uses stolen credentials or application programming interface keys to run AI workloads and leaves the business holding the bill.
Claims brought by customers fall on the third-party side. Cowbell’s example there is a bookkeeping firm whose agent files client tax return…

articles.title: Who Pays for AI Data Center Power Costs? How the U.S. and China Compare - EE Times

In 40 of 41 local ballot contests across 10 U.S. states on Nov. 3, voters favored limiting data center development.
The measures included bans, moratoriums, rejected zoning proposals, and nonbinding votes. Their legal consequences vary, but they signal growing scrutiny of the electricity, land, and public resources required by large computing facilities.
Meanwhile, developers are competing to secure power capacity years before their facilities will operate.
The U.S. relies on utilities, regulators, and local governments to negotiate these commitments. China coordinates computing infrastructure and energy resources through national development programs.
Both face the same uncertainty: How much infrastructure should be built before future computing demand is known, and who pays when forecasts prove wrong?
Computing moves faster than the grid
The International Energy Agency projects global data center electricity consumption rising from approximately 485 terawatt-hours in 2025 to 950 TWh by 2030. Consumption at AI-focused facilities is expected to triple.
AI accelerator generations change within years. Substations, transformers, and transmission connections are designed to operate for decades. Utilities must therefore finance long-lived infrastructure against demand forecasts shaped by a much faster technology cycle.

Kora builds AI models and agents into a new Linux OS bound for Qualcomm Snapdragon PCs
Desktop software company Kora Systems Inc. today unveiled Kora, a Linux-based operating system that builds artificial intelligence models and agents into the system itself.
Qualcomm Technologies Inc. has spent close to a year working with the company to bring it to Snapdragon-powered PCs.
The launch goes after what Kora sees as a ceiling on AI in current desktop computers. Most AI software on macOS and Windows runs inside a browser tab or an app sandbox, according to the company, with little view of the computer underneath.
Because both platforms are closed, Kora argues, the integration stops at that point. Linux, by Kora’s account, is the only operating system open enough to be rebuilt around models and agents from the kernel up.
The core of that rebuild is an inference engine Kora calls Cortex. It pools the central processor, graphics processor and neural processing unit in a PC, plus any other machines on the network, and treats them as one computer. Models run locally on the user’s hardware by default, and frontier models get pulled in for heavier jobs.
On screen, the usual layout of folders and apps is gone. What Kora calls neural workspaces take its place, each one arranged around the task a user is working on. articles.title: Chrome : le mode Incognito va lui aussi vous empêcher de visiter un site frauduleux
articles.summary:
Google ne rate jamais une occasion de rappeler que son navigateur Chrome vérifie en temps réel la dangerosité des sites visités par ses utilisateurs. Mais ce dispositif n’est pas disponible en navigation privée, ni en mode invité. Les choses devraient prochainement changer.
Selon la documentation de Google, la navigation privée de Chrome ne bénéficie pas toujours des mêmes vérifications Safe Browsing que la navigation classique. Elle se contente d’une liste stockée sur l’appareil.
Pourquoi la liste locale ne suffit pas face à des sites éphémères
Safe Browsing repose sur deux mécanismes. Le premier est une liste d’adresses connues comme dangereuses (hameçonnage, logiciels malveillants), stockée sur l’appareil. Le second est une vérification en temps réel. Dans ce cas, Chrome interroge Google pour savoir si l’adresse visitée figure parmi les menaces recensées à cet instant. Avec la protection standard, réglage par défaut, le navigateur consulte d’abord une liste locale de sites réputés sûrs avant de lancer cette requête, laquelle passe par un serveur de confidentialité chargé de masquer l'adresse IP de l’utilisateur.
En mode Incognito, Chrome peut se replier sur la seule liste locale des sites dangereux. Pour éviter de se faire repérer, de nombreux sites malveillants restent en ligne moins de 10 minutes. Or Google précisait par le passé que cette liste est actualisée toutes les 30 à 60 minutes. Une page d’hameçonnage peut donc apparaître et disparaître entre deux mises à jour. …

Many AI companies and evaluation entities already have their own rating systems, but the FMF intends for its scale to be a cross-vendor standard that teams developing patches can rely on.

David Turturean, a recent MIT graduate and a member of the technical staff at the startup lab Physical Superintelligence (PSI), used early access to Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model to solve an 18-year-old problem about quantum computing.
“I’m totally accepting the idea that this might be the last paper I ever put out,” Turturean, who deferred plans to pursue a master’s at MIT’s prestigious computer science and AI lab to join PSI, told TechCrunch. “In a few months, like, why would you even put out a paper?”
The problem in question, the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, concerns the ability of quantum computers to solve problems faster than classical ones. Scott Aaronson, one of the two researchers who posed the problem, writes that he doesn’t quite understand the proof but that he believes it’s correct because it was autoformalized in Lean, a coding language for math, and explained by a team of top researchers with whom PSI shared the solution.
The solution appears to close the door on one avenue quantum computers could follow to solve certain difficult problems at high speed, but not all of them. “It’s a negative result that allows people to know, okay, we’re no longer looking there,” Turturean said.
More broadly, it reflects the upheaval in the scientific world caused by AI problem-solving.

articles.title: Google DeepMind usó IA para verificar matemáticamente la seguridad del cifrado de Signal
articles.summary:
Investigadores de Google DeepMind usaron inteligencia artificial para demostrar con matemáticas varias garantías clave del protocolo criptográfico de Signal, la tecnología que protege los mensajes de esa aplicación. Según informó Wired, el proyecto duró cuatro semanas y no encontró vulnerabilidades nuevas en las partes analizadas.
El trabajo usó un sistema nuevo de la compañía llamado AlphaProof Code. Los investigadores lo describen como una prueba de concepto, es decir, un ensayo para mostrar que la idea funciona antes de aplicarla a gran escala.
La técnica se llama verificación formal: en lugar de probar un programa con ejemplos y esperar que no falle, se escribe en lenguaje matemático lo que el programa debe cumplir y se demuestra que lo cumple. Para quienes trabajan en seguridad informática, según Wired, es una meta largamente buscada.
Hasta ahora, describir esas propiedades y armar la demostración consumía mucho tiempo de especialistas. Un agente de IA, un asistente que ejecuta tareas por su cuenta, acorta sobre todo la segunda parte, la de construir la prueba.
Qué se comprobó y qué quedó fuera
El análisis no incluyó toda la aplicación móvil de Signal, sino ciertas garantías de su protocolo. Los investigadores también probaron la herramienta con versiones antiguas de Signal que tenían fallas conocidas y ya corregidas: el sistema las detectó y mostró que esas versiones no podían verificarse.

articles.title: Hedra's new Model Factory cranks up the production volume for physical AI model training - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Hedra’s new Model Factory cranks up the production volume for physical AI model training
Autonomous artificial intelligence agents have been a massive hit in the digital realm, and now a startup called Hedra Inc. is hoping to take the next step with physical AI systems that can automate tasks in the real world too.
The company today announced the Hedra Model Factory, a new post-training and inference platform that enables the recursive self-improvement of AI models, or RSI for short, designed specifically to power autonomous robots and other machines.
Hedra says that physical AI requires a very different and more specialized form of intelligence that can enable robots and other real-world hardware systems to perform very specific tasks, such as packing irregular-shaped parcels onto palettes. One of the main challenges of physical AI is that each robot and each task it performs requires a different model.
But training all of those models is not feasible, given the vast amounts of data required to create them. That’s why Hedra wants to use RSI to adapt existing models to new tasks.
RSI is a relatively new technique in AI that describes systems that can autonomously evaluate, train and then improve their own architectures. There has been a lot of research into these systems in frontier AI labs, but until now no one has managed to apply that continuous loop to the physical world.
